title: Finite geometrically reduced schemes over fields are etale
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a finite morphism of schemes. Assume $T$ is geometrically reduced over $k$: $T\times_k L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/k$. Then $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale. The empty scheme is allowed. No perfectness assumption on $k$ is imposed.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-base-change], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field, combined with algebra.tex Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions: reduced Artinian components are fields and geometric reducedness makes their finite residue extensions separable. Agent synthesis.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $k$, where $A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. Apply geometric reducedness to $L=k$ to see that $T$ is reduced. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], its global section ring $A$ is reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], $A$ is Artinian.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), reduction to an affine coordinate algebra; Algebra Tag 00J6, finite-dimensional algebras are Artinian

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to $A$. Enumerate its finitely many maximal ideals by $1,\ldots,n$, and put $K_i=A/\mathfrak m_i$, with $k$-structure given by the quotient. The resulting isomorphism $A\cong\prod_i K_i$ respects $k$ because its components are precisely these quotient maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields], the spectra of the projections identify $\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ with pairwise disjoint open singletons covering $T$. Thus $T\cong\coprod_i\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ over $k$: gluing the displayed isomorphisms of disjoint open subschemes gives the isomorphism, with inverse defined on each open summand.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field); Artinian structure theorem, Algebra Tag 00JB

proof.text: Each $K_i$ is finite-dimensional over $k$: the images of a finite $k$-basis of $A$ span its quotient $K_i$. The structural map $k\to K_i$ is injective, since its kernel is an ideal of the field $k$ and cannot contain $1$ in the nonzero field $K_i$. Consequently every $K_i/k$ is a finite field extension.

Choose an algebraic closure $\bar k/k$, whose existence is included in [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change] with base ring $k$, extension ring $\bar k$, and the decomposition in step 2. It identifies $T_{\bar k}$ with $\coprod_i\operatorname{Spec}(K_i\otimes_k\bar k)$. By hypothesis $T_{\bar k}$ is reduced. Each summand is open, and [def-pc-reduced-scheme] says the sections on every open are reduced. Hence $K_i\otimes_k\bar k$ is reduced. Apply [lem-pc-finite-extension-tensor-algebraic-closure-reduced-separable] to conclude that each finite $K_i/k$ is separable. In the terminology of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], take the finitely generated subextension to be $K_i$ itself (a finite vector-space basis generates it as a field); its transcendence basis is empty because it is algebraic. Thus this is separable algebraic, as needed for the next step.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), separability of finite residue extensions; Algebra Tag 030W and the finite-extension algebraic-closure test

proof.text: By [lem-exc-etale-coproduct-etale], the coproduct of the spectra of the finite separable extensions $K_i/k$ is etale over $k$. Under the isomorphism over $k$ of step 2 this is exactly $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, proving the claim. If $A=0$, its maximal-ideal set is empty and the coproduct is empty; the same cited coproduct statement permits an empty index set. No perfectness of $k$ entered any step.
